transcript.text: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there

E:15 means the dishwasher’s anti-flood system has operated. The constantly running pump is expected in that condition: it is trying to protect the machine, not necessarily a failed drain pump. Close the water tap feeding the dishwasher and do not keep trying programmes, as the underlying leak may continue to wet the base. Turning it off and on will not clear it while the base remains wet. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Open the door and inspect the rubber seal all around the tub edge for food debris, splits or flattened areas. Clean off any debris with a damp cloth.
2. Check the lower spray arm turns freely and is not cracked or split. Also check that no tall item in the lower basket could have stopped it or deflected water at the door. If the seal and spray arm look sound, or the fault returns after drying/clearing, it needs an appliance engineer to locate the internal leak. Do not treat drying the base tray as a repair: it may run briefly, then E:15 will return if the leak source remains.

Door seal looks okay and the filter's fairly clean. I can see a bit of water shining in the base tray through a gap by the plinth, but I can't pull the unit out as it's fitted. Is there anything else I can check from the front?

1. Switch it off and unplug it. Remove the lower basket and turn the lower spray arm by hand. Check it is not catching on anything and inspect its underside and ends for a split or crack. A damaged arm can jet water towards the door and end up in the base tray. 2. Close the door and look along its edges against the surrounding unit. It should sit level and evenly closed, without one corner sitting proud or needing lifting to latch. Also make sure no tall item or tray has been able to foul the lower spray arm or direct water at the door. The water visible in the base explains both E:15 and the pump running continuously; the flood protection is doing its job, rather than pointing to a failed drain pump. If the spray arm is sound and the door sits square, the most likely causes are an internal sump/pump seal or hose connection. Those need the integrated dishwasher pulled out and inspected with the water isolated, so an appliance engineer is the sensible next step. Keep the water tap to the dishwasher closed and do not run further cycles.

candidates: Anti-flood protection triggered by water in the base tray (high)
Leak from the door seal, misaligned door, or a damaged/obstructed spray arm (medium)
Internal leak from a pump seal, sump or hose connection (medium)
